chapter: Later views and life in Dallas
title: Gangsters as friends of musicians
summary: Smith ate spaghetti at the Cherry Blossom owners' home, never saw gang rivalry, and had not heard the Jesse Price story.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Just one other thing. In the days when you were... Well, even here in Dallas. But in the 30's and 40's, a lot of the clubs were run by gangsters.
Oh yes.
Did you ever have any incidents with them?
No. I used to eat dinner at a gangster's house.
Which one was that?

In Kansas City. I can't think of their name, but they were one of the two who ran that Cherry Blossom there where we played at, Bennie Moten's band there and Basie and all those. They had the biggest, finest place there was in town up there on
Buster Smith - 221

Vine. Yeah, up on Vine there. And two of them that lived down there in the Italian part of town down there. And they invited me down every night to eat spaghetti, then they'd give me a cigar... They'd give me them cigars they smoked that looked like a corkscrew. Soaked in wine. Yeah, best cigar you ever smoked.
Really?
Yeah.
They were good to musicians, were they?

Yeah. That's the musician's friend. Sure. Them gangsters, all you did was tend your business and then... You couldn't reach them nohow. You just tend to your business. A musician ain't nothin' when you come around them gangsters. He's ain't nothin'. All he do is entertain the folks. You can't step in his business.
Did you ever see any examples of rivalry between gangsters? Like one lot shooting up the other lot?
No, no. I never ran into that.
I believe there was one incident in Kansas City where something went wrong, and one lot of gangsters... Some club owners stepped out of line, and the gangsters took him out and shot him.
Yeah.
They made the band in the place come out and watch the shooting. Did you ever hear about it?
Buster Smith - 222
No, I haven't heard about that. It might have been, but I never heard...
It's in Ross Russell's book about Charlie Parker. I can't remember which band it was. There was one incident like that.
I don't know. It's the first of me hearing. It wasn't Jap Allen. George Lee? Clarence Love? Andy Kirk? Bennie Moten? Blue Devils?
No, it wasn't any of those. [JESSE PRICE]
No, it wasn't any of those.
[AGAIN, SEE RUSSELL, JAZZ STYLES IN KANSAS CITY AND THE SOUTHWEST, PAGE 22, CITED ABOVE IN TRANSCRIPT.]
